title: ICMPv4 header
summary: An ICMPv4 message begins with an 8-byte header: type (1 byte), code (1 byte), checksum (2 bytes), then type-specific data (4 bytes, e.g. identifier + sequence number for echo). Common types: 0 echo reply, 3 destination unreachable, 8 echo request, 11 time exceeded.

ext.summary: An ICMPv4 message begins with an 8-byte header: type (1 byte), code (1 byte), checksum (2 bytes), then type-specific data (4 bytes, e.g. identifier + sequence number for echo). Common types: 0 echo reply, 3 destination unreachable, 8 echo request, 11 time exceeded.

structure.meaning: Message type: 0 echo reply, 3 dest unreachable, 5 redirect, 8 echo request, 11 time exceeded, 12 parameter problem.
Sub-type (e.g. 3/0 = net unreachable, 3/1 = host unreachable, 11/0 = TTL exceeded in transit).
ICMP checksum (one's complement of one's complement sum of the whole ICMP message).
Type-specific: for echo (type 0/8) = identifier (2) + sequence number (2); for others = unused/zero.
Payload (echo data, or the original IP header + 8 bytes of the offending datagram for errors).

ext.example_decoded: Echo request (type 8), code 0, id 1, seq 1, payload 'Hello'
notes: ICMP rides directly on IP (protocol 1), not on TCP/UDP.
Echo request/reply (ping) uses type 8/0 with matching identifier and sequence number.
Destination unreachable (type 3) includes the original IP header + first 8 bytes of the offending datagram.
Checksum covers the ICMP message only (not the IP header, unlike TCP/UDP which include a pseudo-header).
Path MTU discovery uses type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed) with the MTU in the rest-of-header field.
